transcript.purpose: The live dictation filling the top of the card; settled text in Silk-Screen Ivory, streaming tail in Raw Warm.

status.purpose: The machine display's line over the tape window, with a faint VFD warmth.

detail.purpose: Secondary status line in Unlit Ivory, ellipsized.

note-body.purpose: The update service note's secondary line in Unlit Ivory.

legend.purpose: The printed micro-legend under the lamp (REC/BUSY/DONE/ERR) — the only uppercase in the world.

counter.purpose: The monospace take counter, tabular-nums; digits dim to 45% opacity outside recording.

shadows.name: recessed-well
shadows.purpose: Wells sunk into the faceplate: the tape window and the counter cell.

shadows.name: machined-edge-card
shadows.purpose: The card's machined top edge — an inset highlight, not a cast shadow.

shadows.name: machined-edge-key
shadows.purpose: The inset top light on machined key caps.

shadows.name: lamp-bloom-rec
shadows.purpose: The lit recording lamp's bloom — the material of a lit lamp, not elevation.

shadows.name: service-lamp-bloom
shadows.purpose: The 7px amber service lamp on the update note.

shadows.name: key-backlight
shadows.purpose: The backlit STOP key while there's a take to stop; hover raises alpha to 0.5.

shadows.name: playhead-glow
shadows.purpose: The glowing playhead riding the progress fill's leading edge.

shadows.name: raw-warmth
shadows.purpose: Text-shadow warmth on the fresh raw transcript tail.

shadows.name: vfd-warmth
shadows.purpose: Text-shadow on the machine display's status line — display glass, not decoration.

motion.name: key-state
motion.purpose: Key and surface state changes: background, box-shadow, color.

motion.name: surface-fade
motion.purpose: Grip opacity and the written tape dimming to a backdrop.

motion.name: progress-linear
motion.purpose: Progress fill width, tape-window playhead and update bar alike; completed bars hold 400ms then hide.

motion.name: card-height
motion.purpose: The card eases its own height while the native window snaps.

motion.name: pulse-starting
motion.purpose: The hollow REC ring while the mic warms up.

motion.name: spin-supply
motion.purpose: The supply reel while recording; paused (keeping its angle) otherwise.

motion.name: spin-takeup
motion.purpose: The take-up reel turns a touch faster — the asymmetry that reads as a machine.

motion.name: spin-processing
motion.purpose: Reels reading the tape back during transcribing/cleaning; delivering runs 1.4s.

motion.name: tape-speed
motion.purpose: The write clock: one oxide column per 80ms of captured audio, gliding between writes.

motion.name: reduced-motion-collapse
motion.value: transition-duration 0.01ms; animation: none; tape steps without glide
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion the tape still updates (state, not decoration) but all glide, pulse, and spin collapse.

components.name: Transport Key
components.description: A machined 34px key cap with inset top light and a ~42px invisible hit halo; the press travels.
components.html: <button class="ds-key" aria-label="Key"><svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" width="14" height="14" aria-hidden="true"><rect x="3" y="3" width="10" height="10" rx="2" fill="currentColor"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-key { position: relative; width: 34px; height: 34px; border-radius: 9px; border: 1px solid rgba(255, 240, 214, 0.12); cursor: pointer; padding: 0; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; background: #2a2118; color: #f2e9da; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255, 240, 214, 0.07); transition: background 0.12s ease, box-shadow 0.12s ease, color 0.12s ease, transform 0.08s ease; } .ds-key::before { content: ""; position: absolute; inset: -4px; border-radius: 12px; } .ds-key svg { display: block; } .ds-key:hover { background: #342a1e; } .ds-key:active { transform: translateY(1px) scale(0.96); } .ds-key:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #f2e9da; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Backlit Stop Key
components.description: The STOP key, backlit red while there's a take to stop — the machine telling you which key it expects.
components.html: <button class="ds-key-stop" title="Stop and transcribe" aria-label="Stop and transcribe"><svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" width="14" height="14" aria-hidden="true"><rect x="3" y="3" width="10" height="10" rx="2" fill="currentColor"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-key-stop { position: relative; width: 34px; height: 34px; border-radius: 9px; border: 1px solid rgba(255, 68, 56, 0.5); cursor: pointer; padding: 0; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; background: #3a1611; color: #ffb4ac; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255, 240, 214, 0.06), 0 0 10px rgba(255, 68, 56, 0.35); transition: background 0.12s ease, box-shadow 0.12s ease, transform 0.08s ease; } .ds-key-stop::before { content: ""; position: absolute; inset: -4px; border-radius: 12px; } .ds-key-stop svg { display: block; } .ds-key-stop:hover { background: #4a1b14; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255, 240, 214, 0.06), 0 0 10px rgba(255, 68, 56, 0.5); } .ds-key-stop:active { transform: translateY(1px) scale(0.96); } .ds-key-stop:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #f2e9da; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Eject Key
components.description: Cancel discards the take, like pulling the tape; the glyph sits in Unlit Ivory, warming on hover, offset an extra 4px from STOP.
components.html: <button class="ds-key-eject" title="Cancel — discard the recording" aria-label="Cancel"><svg viewBox="0 0 16 16" width="13" height="13" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M8 3.2 L12.8 9 H3.2 Z" fill="currentColor"/><rect x="3.2" y="10.8" width="9.6" height="2" rx="1" fill="currentColor"/></svg></button>

components.name: Counter Cell
components.description: A recessed monospace counter that counts captured audio only; digits go unlit (45%) when not running.
components.css: .ds-counter { min-width: 52px; height: 30px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; background: #0f0c09; border-radius: 6px; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 3px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.55); } .ds-counter-digits { font-family: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Code', monospace; font-size: 13px; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; letter-spacing: 0.04em; color: #f2e9da; }

components.name: Tape Window
components.description: The hero: a recessed well the umber ribbon runs through, oxide signal written at the fixed record head (40%) sliding toward the take-up reel.
components.css: .ds-tape-window { position: relative; width: 220px; height: 34px; background: #0f0c09; border-radius: 6px; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 3px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.55); overflow: hidden; } .ds-tape-ribbon { position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; top: 50%; height: 18px; transform: translateY(-50%); background: #35291d; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4), inset 0 -1px 0 rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4); } .ds-tape-signal { position: absolute; left: 40%; right: 0; top: 6px; bottom: 6px; background: repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(210, 154, 90, 0.9) 0 1.5px, transparent 1.5px 2.5px); -webkit-mask-image: linear-gradient(180deg, transparent 0, #000 20%, #000 80%, transparent 100%); mask-image: linear-gradient(180deg, transparent 0, #000 20%, #000 80%, transparent 100%); } .ds-tape-head { position: absolute; left: 40%; top: 2px; bottom: 2px; width: 1px; background: rgba(242, 233, 218, 0.45); } .ds-tape-head::before { content: ""; position: absolute; top: -2px; left: -2px; width: 5px; height: 6px; border-radius: 0 0 2px 2px; background: #b4a894; opacity: 0.8; }

components.name: Lamp Block
components.description: An 11px status lamp with its printed micro-legend; shown lit REC with bloom and pulse — the filled lamp means samples are flowing.
components.css: .ds-lamp { display: inline-flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 3px; width: 30px; padding: 6px; background: #1c1713; border-radius: 6px; } .ds-lamp-dot { width: 11px; height: 11px; border-radius: 50%; background: #ff4438; box-shadow: 0 0 9px 1px rgba(255, 68, 56, 0.5); animation: ds-pulse 2s ease-in-out infinite; } .ds-lamp-legend { font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; font-size: 8px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.08em; color: #ff958c; } @keyframes ds-pulse { 0%, 100% { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1); } 50% { opacity: 0.45; transform: scale(0.82); } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-lamp-dot { animation: none; } }

narrative.overview:
Earheart's overlay is a machine you can watch working: a miniature reel-to-reel lying along the bottom of the screen. Dictation is not a pulsing dot in a pill — it is signal being physically written onto moving tape. The world is a warm-black instrument faceplate with wells sunk into it: an umber tape ribbon carrying the oxide-written waveform past a fixed record head, aluminum reels whose hub windows make rotation visible, a mechanical counter, legended status lamps, and machined transport keys. A glance tells the whole story: lamp lit, reels turning, your words being written onto tape and appearing above; the backlit square key stops, eject discards.

The finish is flat matte throughout. The only glow in the world comes from things that are lit — status lamps, the backlit STOP key, the playhead — never from ambience. Depth is machined into the faceplate (inset wells, inset top highlights), never cast under it: the overlay window is transparent, and a drop shadow would band and halo against the desktop. Motion is mechanical physics, not decoration: reels spin at different speeds, keys travel when pressed, tape glides at a fixed write speed, and all of it collapses to instant state changes under prefers-reduced-motion. Text is quiet system UI silk-screened in ivory onto the faceplate; the machine's own numerals are monospace.

Confirmed rejections, from the shipped overlay itself: no cast shadows on the transparent window; no translucent surface under text (the faceplate is solid so the written tape and the warm raw tail never depend on what shows through behind the overlay); no category-standard pulsing-dot pill.

Legacy note: the settings window and setup wizard (renderer/settings.css, renderer/wizard.css) still ship the previous violet-black / rose "On-Air Lamp" system and have not yet migrated. New surfaces follow the Tape Transport world; settings and wizard carry the legacy system pending migration. Never blend the two worlds on one surface.
keyCharacteristics: Interface as instrument: every state is a lamp, a reel speed, or a written trace — never an abstract spinner.
Warm-black and oxide materials; saturated color exists only in lamps.
Depth by inset: wells sink into the faceplate; nothing floats above it.
Glow means lit: lamp blooms and key backlight are the world's only shadows.
Honest state: the machine never claims to be listening before samples flow.

rules.name: The Lamp Vocabulary Rule
rules.body: Status colors are a fixed legended vocabulary: REC red = capturing, BUSY amber = working (or the machine talking about itself), DONE green = delivered, inert warm grey = idle or fault. Never repurpose a lamp color for decoration, and never invent a second color for a meaning that already has a lamp.

rules.name: The Oxide-Is-Material Rule
rules.body: The written trace is Oxide — muted, material, the take itself. Saturated red is reserved for the REC lamp and the backlit STOP key. If the tape glows lamp-red, the lamp means nothing.

rules.name: The Machine-Numerals Rule
rules.body: Anything the machine counts — the take counter — is monospace with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums, seated in a recessed cell. Human words are never monospace.

rules.name: The Depth-Is-Inset Rule
rules.body: The overlay window is transparent, and soft shadows band and halo on transparent windows — so the card carries no drop shadow, ever. Depth is machined into the faceplate instead: wells recess (inset 0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,0.55)), edges catch light as inset top highlights, and the card's lift comes from its solid surface and hairline Machine Edge border. Every outward glow in the system is a lit thing, not elevation.

rules.name: The Keys-Stay-In-Their-Slots Rule
rules.body: A machine doesn't remove its keys. Keys that don't currently apply go unlit and inert — visibility/state, not display — so neighboring keys never jump.

rules.name: The Filled-Lamp Contract
rules.body: The lit pulsing lamp + written tape + running counter mean "audio is being captured right now." While the mic warms up the lamp is a hollow ring — the card only promises it's getting there. Never show the filled lamp before samples flow.

dos: Do keep the lamp vocabulary fixed: REC red capturing, BUSY amber working or self-referential, DONE green delivered, inert warm grey for idle/fault (The Lamp Vocabulary Rule).
Do express depth by inset — recessed wells (inset 0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,0.55)) and inset top lights — and reserve outward glow for lit things: lamp blooms, key backlight, the playhead.

Do keep motion mechanical and honest: 0.12s ease for key/surface states, 0.08s key travel, 0.15s linear progress, 0.18s card height, 0.2s card entrance; reels pause (keeping their angle) rather than reset; collapse everything under prefers-reduced-motion while still updating state.
Do paint 34px keys but offer ~42px hit areas (inset −4px pseudo-element), and isolate destructive keys with extra gap.
Do set machine numerals in monospace tabular-nums, and dim (never hide) readouts that aren't running.
Do keep the faceplate solid; text and tape must never depend on what shows through behind the transparent window.
donts: Don't cast a shadow on the overlay card — soft shadows band and halo on transparent windows; depth is inset, never cast (The Depth-Is-Inset Rule).
Don't paint the written tape in lamp red — the trace is muted Oxide; saturated red belongs to the REC lamp and the backlit STOP key (The Oxide-Is-Material Rule).
Don't show the filled recording lamp before samples flow — warming up is a hollow ring (The Filled-Lamp Contract).
Don't remove keys that don't apply — unlit and inert in their slots, so the eject key never jumps (The Keys-Stay-In-Their-Slots Rule).
Don't blend worlds: settings/wizard carry the legacy On-Air Lamp system pending migration; new surfaces are Tape Transport only, and no surface mixes the two palettes.
Don't invite the user to talk before the mic is live — the card says "Starting mic…" until the first samples arrive.
